record.paper_title: Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies
record.original_question: Which accelerator, fixed-target, forward-physics, and air-shower measurements are needed to improve hadronic-interaction models enough to reduce systematic uncertainties in ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray mass-composition inference, especially for pion-proton, kaon-proton, pion-light-nuclei, kaon-light-nuclei, proton-oxygen, and forward secondary-particle production?

evidence.quote: An important aspect of the hadronic interaction models is the extrapolation of accelerator data to center-of-mass energies of up to √s ∼ 400 TeV , well beyond energies accessible at colliders, to forward phase space regions not accessible in experiments, and to projectile and target particle combinations not measured in accelerator experiments.
Additional data from collider and ﬁxed-target experiments and progress in the theory and phenomenology of multiparticle production are required to lower these uncertainties.
Of prime importance are the measurement of the pion-proton, kaon-proton, pion-light-nuclei, and kaon-light-nuclei cross sections and the corresponding distributions of leading secondary particles.
Taking data of proton-oxygen at LHC is technically possible and would be a key measurement for improving air shower predictions.
Closely related to this transition between two regimes is the question of non-linear effects, or even parton density saturation, expected at very high parton densities.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the study of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays (with primary energies extending up to center-of-mass nucleon-nucleon energies of order √s ∼ 400 TeV), the inference of the mass composition of primary cosmic rays from extensive air-shower observables (such as the depth of shower maximum X_max and its fluctuations, muon content, and longitudinal profile) is limited by systematic uncertainties in hadronic-interaction Monte Carlo models. These models must extrapolate accelerator data to (i) center-of-mass energies far beyond those accessible at current colliders, (ii) forward phase-space regions (large pseudorapidity / large Feynman-x) not covered by central detectors, and (iii) projectile–target combinations not measured experimentally.

Identify and specify a concrete program of accelerator (collider), fixed-target, forward-physics, and air-shower measurements that would, if carried out, reduce these systematic uncertainties to a level sufficient for unambiguous mass-composition inference at ultrahigh energies. In particular, determine the required measurements (energy ranges, kinematic coverage, and observables — total and inelastic cross sections together with leading-secondary momentum and multiplicity distributions) for each of the following interaction channels:

1. pion–proton (π–p),
2. kaon–proton (K–p),
3. pion–light-nuclei (π–A, with A a light nucleus such as carbon, nitrogen, or oxygen),
4. kaon–light-nuclei (K–A),
5. proton–oxygen (p–O), including the feasibility and benefit of running such collisions at the LHC,
6. forward secondary-particle production (production spectra of π^±, K^±, K_L, neutrons, protons, and Λ at large Feynman-x in proton–proton, proton–nucleus, and pion–nucleus collisions).

For each channel, state the kinematic coverage (√s, x_F or pseudorapidity, p_T) needed, and quantify how the resulting reduction in uncertainty of the predicted air-shower observables would translate into improved discrimination among primary mass groups (proton, helium, CNO, iron) at energies E ≳ 10^18 eV.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a programmatic open question in ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray physics. Several of the requested measurements are being pursued (e.g., the LHCf forward measurements, the LHC oxygen-beam run planned/performed in Run 3, NA61/SHINE pion-carbon data), but the full program needed to fully resolve hadronic-model uncertainties in mass-composition inference has not been completed, and the question remains active in the field as of 2026.

status_evidence.snippet: Additional data from collider and fixed-target experiments ... are required to lower these uncertainties.
status_evidence.claim: The needed measurements were identified as open requirements.

status_evidence.title: LHC oxygen-oxygen and proton-oxygen runs (LHC Run 3)
status_evidence.snippet: A short pilot p-O and O-O run at the LHC is planned to address cosmic-ray air-shower modeling.
status_evidence.claim: Proton-oxygen at the LHC is being pursued but the full measurement program is incomplete.
